content.title: About
content.content: Glazed cooked carrots are boiled carrot pieces coated with a sweet glaze made from sugar, butter, and sometimes spices. They retain a bright orange color and a tender texture, making them a popular side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Glazed carrots are a classic garnish in many European and American meals.
The sugar in the glaze helps lock in the carrot’s natural sweetness and vivid color.
The "glazed carrots" style became popular in the United States in the early 20th century as a kid‑friendly vegetable preparation.
Carrots are rich in beta‑carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.
Glazing can be done with honey, maple syrup, or orange juice for a flavor twist.

items.title: High in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene supports vision, immune function, and skin health.

items.title: Source of vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C provides antioxidant protection and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: A typical serving (≈100 g) contains about 70 kcal, making it diet‑friendly.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and a feeling of fullness.

items.title: Provides potassium
items.content: Potassium helps maintain normal blood pressure.

items.title: Added sugar
items.content: The glaze adds simple sugars, so people with diabetes should watch portion size.

items.title: Carrot allergy
items.content: Rare, but some individuals may be allergic to carrots.

items.title: Digestive sensitivity
items.content: Large amounts of fiber can cause gas in sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve glazed carrots warm as a side dish with meat, poultry, or fish. They also work well in salads, vegetable casseroles, or as a festive appetizer.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked glazed carrots in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. Reheat gently in a pan or microwave before serving.
